items.title: ATS-010 requires typed, cross-run receipts
items.statement: Discovery through cleanup operations must emit typed receipts linked to project, compile, goal, node, attempt, capability, and source-currentness identities.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: 'Discovery, research, selection, installation, harness probe, visible session, user interaction, test result, artifact, exception, and cleanup operations produce typed receipts linked to project, PlanCompileRun, GoalRun, WorkNode, attempt, capability, and source currentness. Provisioning Preflight confirms that selected test capabilities, installations, services, browsers, devices, simulators, credentials, and commands remain current and runnable immediately before WorkNode execution. Historical quotations, compatibility notes, vendor or third-party sources, generated lockfiles, and rules that mention TODO or stub terminology are not false positives, while empty functions, panic or unimplemented paths, placeholder returns, fake tests, and implement-later prose are blockers. items.title: Typed receipt shape and lifecycle are not specified
items.statement: The receipt requirement identifies producers and linkage targets but does not define receipt fields, type discriminator values, persistence owner, ordering, idempotency, retention, visibility, or how source-currentness changes propagate to prior receipts.
items.impact: Independent builders can emit incompatible receipts and consumers cannot reliably correlate, retain, invalidate, or audit them.
items.builder_discretion: Receipt schemas, storage, lifecycle, ordering, and invalidation semantics remain discretionary.

items.statement: The PlanUnit names the fixture matrix, but its acceptance criteria verify lineage preservation and compile boundaries, and its listed validation surfaces are plan-index and ledger validators rather than the fixture suite itself.
items.impact: ATS-010 can satisfy its declared acceptance surfaces without proving any receipt, preflight, restart, cancellation, or incomplete-item runtime behavior.

items.title: Discovery performance budgets have no thresholds
items.statement: The acceptance criterion enumerates performance surfaces but gives no latency, throughput, memory, disk, timeout, workload-size, percentile, hardware, or concurrency values.
items.impact: Any measured result can be called compliant, and over-budget fallback cannot be triggered consistently.
items.builder_discretion: Builders choose all quantitative budgets and test conditions.

dimension_assessments.summary: Preflight, incomplete-item classification, discovery, History, and vision behaviors are explicitly named.
The window defines broad ATS-010 fixtures and Discovery, History, and vision acceptance capabilities.
Receipts and vision outputs are required, but their schemas, enumerations, and precedence inputs are incomplete.
Typed receipts, consumer conformance, History authority, and vision routing lack exact interoperable contracts.
Several transitions are named, but preflight failure, Discovery fallback, History rebuild, consent revocation, cache, and retry transitions lack complete state machines.
History authority-sensitive actions and vision consent or redaction override do not bind decisions to exact principals and scopes.
Document ownership is explicit, but runtime accountability across implementation surfaces and owner hints is not.
Discovery references every consumer row and receipts reference many link targets, but exact consumer contracts and the receipt consumers themselves are not enumerated here.
Discovery, History, and vision units are explicitly GUI-related, while ATS-010 is explicitly classified as backend workflow behavior.
Vision fail-closed behavior and History rebuild are present, but exact preflight, fallback, rebuild, provider, and cache recovery semantics remain open.
Discovery no-leak coverage is strong, but History redaction and vision consent or override authority remain under-specified.
Receipt source-currentness, stale History state, consent revocation, cache invalidation, and fallback outcomes lack explicit propagation rules.
Immediate preflight and multiple recovery operations are required, but current executable suites and operational limits are absent.
Discovery names performance surfaces without numbers, while History and vision define no quantitative scale budgets.
Compatibility false positives and Discovery cache migration are recognized, but migration outcomes, compatibility versions, and rebuild or discard selection rules are not exact.
Some negative and privacy oracles are precise, but ATS-010, History, and vision rely on structural validators or future suites instead of executable behavior evidence.
Material discretion remains over schemas, owners, thresholds, transition policies, authority, retries, caches, and executable test oracles.
Key terms including current, runnable, reliable, consumer row, authority-sensitive, deterministic precedence, degraded reason, and over-budget are not operationally defined in this core.
